faq: Can you repair old data that was already recorded?
Mostly not. Analytics tools do not let you rewrite history. We fix the problem going forward, add notes on the dates it changed and, where useful, build a corrected view in a report.
How will I know the fix worked?
We compare the numbers to your store's order totals before and after, and show you the difference. A match within a small margin is normal, and we explain any gap that remains.
What if there is more wrong than the package covers?
We tell you after the first day, with a short list and a price to add the extra work. You choose whether to continue. Nothing is billed beyond the order without your yes.
Do you delete anything from my accounts?
We only change settings, tags and filters, and we note every change in the log so it can be reversed. Nothing is permanently deleted without asking, and we export a copy of the old setup first.
desc:
Analytics data cleanup and duplicate removal repairs reports that show too much revenue, doubled sessions or odd referrals. Ecom Swift LLC finds the cause in your accounts, fixes what can be fixed and records every change so your numbers can be trusted.

## Why does messy analytics data matter?

Messy analytics data matters because every business decision built on it inherits the error. If revenue looks higher than your bank deposits, you may overspend on ads that seem to perform. If your own visits and bots fill the traffic report, you may judge a page by people who never meant to buy.

Typical symptoms are easy to spot once you know them. Purchases appear twice. Sessions jump when someone refreshes a thank-you page. Your payment provider shows up as a top referral, which means shoppers who paid are counted as new visitors coming back. Traffic from odd countries arrives in bursts with no orders behind it.

## How cleaner data changes what you can see

Clean data makes trends believable. A conversion rate that includes bot visits is lower than the truth, and a revenue figure that counts orders twice is higher. Fixing both lets you compare channels, pages and months fairly.

Referral problems matter for attribution. When a payment or checkout domain steals credit, the true source of the order, such as search or email, is lost. Repairing cross-domain tracking and referral exclusions puts credit back where it belongs and makes channel reports useful again.

Clean data also protects future work. A new dashboard, an ad audience or a monthly report built on faulty numbers repeats the fault. Cleanup comes first.

## What a proper cleanup covers

- A review of the analytics property, its data streams and its settings.
- Detection of duplicate tags, such as the same analytics code installed by a theme and a tag manager.
- Removal of duplicate purchase events, using the order ID to confirm the fix.
- Filters for internal traffic, so staff and developer visits stop counting.
- Handling of spam and bot traffic where it can be separated from real visitors.
- Referral exclusions for payment gateways and checkout domains.
- Cross-domain setup repaired where your store spans more than one domain.
- Consistent naming for campaign links, so sources are not split into near copies.
- Annotations on the dates when each change took effect.
- A before and after summary, and a log of every action.

## How we approach the work

We begin by reading the symptoms you describe and comparing your analytics with your store. A mismatch between orders and tracked purchases tells us where to look first. Then we inspect the site with a browser inspector and a tag debugging tool, list every tag that fires and read the property's settings.

When we find a cause, we change it in your accounts and test it with a real action. Each fix is dated, and we add an annotation so anyone reading the report later can see where behavior shifted. This is important, because a repaired setup breaks the line between old and new data and you do not want a drop in numbers to look like a business problem.

The Basic package targets the main cause of wrong numbers on one property. Standard widens the cleanup to duplicate sales and referral problems. Premium compares analytics, ad accounts and your store, repairs cross-domain tracking, tidies campaign naming and includes a check two weeks after the fixes. If we find more than the package covers, we say so and describe what remains.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a note of every tracking change, with the date.
- Compare analytics purchases with store orders after each fix.
- Filter out your own team's visits.
- Use one naming style for campaign links.
- Ask for a recheck after a theme or checkout update.

**Avoid:**
- Deleting data you might need later.
- Fixing several things at once without testing each.
- Comparing months before and after a fix without noting the change date.
- Installing a second analytics tag to solve a problem with the first.
- Assuming old, recorded data will correct itself.

## Who needs data cleanup

It suits owners whose analytics revenue does not match their store, agencies inheriting a messy account, and stores that changed theme, checkout or domain and saw reports behave oddly afterward. It is also a sensible step before building dashboards or reports on top of the data.

Data already recorded generally stays as it was, so cleanup mostly improves what is collected from the fix date onward.

## What we need from you

Send us the symptoms you have noticed and a few examples, such as a day when numbers looked wrong. We need editor or administrator access to your analytics property, tag manager and store, given by inviting our email as a user. If ad accounts are involved, viewer access is enough to compare numbers. We never ask for your password, and we delete nothing from your accounts without telling you first.
